title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Price increase (1.5%)
drivers.evidence: Recent weeks at $0.68 show sales near baseline (388–524 units); no historical drop observed.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery warning
drivers.evidence: No past data on delivery shortfalls; only a warning. Risk of stockouts may reduce sales. Noise-adjusted effect shrunk to -5% due to low evidence.

adjustment.analysis: No events are scheduled. The price increased 1.5% to $0.68, which historically has not caused a meaningful drop in sales (recent weeks at $0.68 show 388–524 units, near baseline). The supplier warning of short delivery introduces supply risk, which may suppress demand if stockouts occur. This is a single, untested risk with no prior evidence of impact. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends and recent volatility. The noise-adjusted effect of Halloween is neutral (x1.0), and the classical model’s suggestion of 1.00 is appropriate. The price lift is minor and not historically disruptive. The supply risk is a downside driver with low confidence. No promotion or holiday justifies a multiplier above 1.0.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.2 | 5%-95%: 313.0 - 555.6 | 10%-90%: 346.8 - 528.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
